authorization: Publisher explicitly authorised three verified daily company-analysis articles on 2 November 2026, superseding the repository's one-new-article daily cap.
story_thesis: Positive quarterly cash flow is encouraging, but a durable recovery requires Commercial Airplanes to become profitable, inventory to convert into deliveries and debt to keep falling.

identity.units: USD millions except per-share and aircraft data

duplicate_checks: Checked EDITORIAL_TOPIC_INDEX.md, CONTENT_INVENTORY.md, data/content-inventory.json and actual wealth Markdown; Boeing has a stock profile but no dedicated cash-flow or Commercial Airplanes analysis.
Checked open pull requests 57 and 43 and recently merged publication pull requests; no Boeing article or matching fingerprint was active.
Checked recent company-publication records and live site content before drafting; no 2 November scheduled article slot had been used.
This is a business-economics question, not a routine quarter-by-quarter recap; routine figures remain linked through /stocks/ba/.

evidence_table.claim: Q3 revenue was USD24.188bn, operating cash flow USD1.496bn and Boeing-defined free cash flow USD464m.
evidence_table.result: verified in separate fact-check pass; free cash flow labelled non-GAAP

evidence_table.claim: Nine-month operating cash flow was USD2.681bn, capex USD3.040bn and free cash flow negative USD359m, versus negative USD2.252bn a year earlier.
Commercial Airplanes delivered 161 aircraft, recorded USD10.720bn revenue, a USD697m operating loss and negative 6.5% margin.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Commercial Airplanes segment table and MD&A.
evidence_table.result: verified; delivery mix and production/supply-chain costs attributed to management

evidence_table.claim: Commercial Airplanes' nine-month operating loss narrowed to USD1.582bn from USD6.447bn.
Inventory was USD90.948bn, up USD6.269bn or about 7.4% from USD84.679bn at 2025 year end.
evidence_table.result: verified; article rounds percentage to about 7%

evidence_table.claim: Backlog was USD745.431bn, including USD611.833bn Commercial Airplanes backlog and more than 6,300 commercial aircraft.
Cash and marketable securities were USD20.7bn and debt USD45.9bn, down from USD54.1bn at 2025 year end.
evidence_table.location_or_arithmetic: Release liquidity paragraph and 10-Q debt note.
evidence_table.result: verified; no unsupported net-debt measure used

fact_check_pass.method: After drafting, every material number, period, segment label, accounting measure, management explanation and calculation was reread against the SEC-furnished release and Form 10-Q; arithmetic was recomputed independently.
